title: Instrumentation Horizon Adapter: low-overhead KV context shield and header repair
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight 'Horizon Adapter' instrumentation shim for language SDKs that provides compact binary KV context serialization, opportunistic header repair, and a hot-path tracing hook with <10µs median overhead for typical edge request paths. This ticket covers design, SDK changes (Node/Python/Go), runtime integration tests, benchmarks, rollout, and dashboarding for detection of regressions.

Scope:
- Design a compact binary KV serializer (prefix-free, size-limited) that sits alongside OTLP/traceparent headers and our legacy X-Redwood headers.
- Add an SDK hook (instrumentation.horizon) that: fast-paths when binary KV present; otherwise tries to reconstruct context from multiple legacy headers; falls back to a safe, non-blocking no-op.
- Provide middleware adapters for Express, FastAPI, and gRPC interceptors to attach/detach KV context to requests.
- Implement sampling hint passthrough and a lightweight per-request provenance stamp to aid debug without inflating spans.
- Add unit and e2e tests verifying loss-tolerance (corrupted header), cross-service roundtrip, and interop with OTLP/Jaeger/Elastic ingestion.
- Benchmarks and target: median SDK hook overhead <= 10µs on 4 vCPU hot-path, p95 <= 50µs; binary KV payloads should average <64 bytes for typical traces.
- Rollout: staged canary by traffic tag with auto-rollback on error-rate or latency increase thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs expose instrumentation.horizon hook with same surface across Node/Python/Go.
- Binary serializer documented and backwards-compatible with existing collectors.
- Performance measurements attached to PR and infra benchmarks.
- Console dashboards updated: per-route instrumentation overhead, header-repair counts, and KV payload size distribution.
- Security review completed (KMS treatment of any sensitive KV fields, header integrity checks).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after spike with prototype binary serializer. Spike showed 6.2µs median hook overhead on Node baseline. Attached prototype gist and notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Horizon+Adapter+Spike

2025-02-14 - Luca Fernandez: Design doc uploaded (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Horizon+Adapter+Design. Key trade-offs called out: avoid runtime allocations on hot-path, prefer fixed-size buffer pooling over per-request allocs, and limit repair heuristics to max 3 attempts to bound CPU cost.
2025-02-16 - QA: Added test plan for corrupted headers and missing KV payloads. Found an edge case in Python tracing where context GC caused transient nil references; assigned follow-up to ENG-71124.

2025-02-18 - Performance: Microbenchmarks (Node v18) added to CI. Results: median hook 5.8µs, p95 28µs with pooling enabled. Go implementation initial run shows median 3.4µs. Uploaded benchmark artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/horizon/benchmarks/ENG-71123/

2025-02-20 - PM review (Arman Singh): Reviewed rollout and dashboards. Requested an additional metric: header-repair-rate per region and a dashboard alert if repair-rate > 0.5% for >5m. Added label 'edge' for targeted canary region rollout.

2025-02-20 - Security (Priya Rao): Quick review requested on storage of provenance stamp. Recommended deterministic HMAC for integrity and guidance on masking fields prior to logging. Security review required flag set.
Next steps: finalize serializer spec, implement Node/Python/Go SDK hooks, add middleware adapters, wire ingestion tests with collector team, and prepare canary config (5% -> 25% -> 75%).
